concern_addon_notes.Acne marks: These are likely post-inflammatory marks left behind after acne has healed. They usually fade on their own over months, but a brightening ingredient like niacinamide, azelaic acid, or vitamin C can speed this up - and daily SPF is essential, since sun exposure darkens these marks further and can make them long-lasting.
concern_addon_notes.Blackheads: Blackheads are open, oxidized clogs rather than true whiteheads. A BHA (salicylic acid) used consistently 3-4x a week is more effective long-term than pore strips or manual extraction, which only give temporary results and can cause irritation or scarring if done at home.
concern_addon_notes.Breakouts: Frequent or recurring breakouts suggest your current routine or a specific trigger (a new product, diet, stress, or your hormonal cycle) may be aggravating your skin. Try tracking what changed around when they started, and introduce one new active ingredient at a time so you can identify what actually helps.
concern_addon_notes.Clogged pores: Clogged pores are the earliest stage before blackheads or whiteheads fully form. Regular but gentle exfoliation with a BHA, plus avoiding heavy, comedogenic products, helps prevent them from progressing into visible breakouts.
concern_addon_notes.Dark spots: Dark spots typically respond best to a combination of a tyrosinase-inhibiting ingredient (alpha arbutin, niacinamide, or azelaic acid) and strict daily sunscreen - without consistent SPF, spots can persist indefinitely or return after treatment.
concern_addon_notes.Dry cheeks: Localized dryness on the cheeks, especially alongside oilier areas elsewhere, points toward combination skin rather than all-over dryness. Apply a richer, ceramide-based moisturizer specifically to these areas rather than across the whole face.
concern_addon_notes.Dry patches: Persistent dry, flaky patches that don't respond to regular moisturizer can indicate a compromised skin barrier. Scale back active ingredients (retinoids, acids) temporarily and focus on ceramide- and hyaluronic-acid-based repair products until the patches resolve.
concern_addon_notes.Excess oil: Excess oil doesn't mean you should skip moisturizer - doing so often triggers your skin to produce even more oil to compensate. A lightweight, oil-free, niacinamide-based moisturizer regulates output more effectively than stripping the skin.
concern_addon_notes.Fine lines: Fine lines are often the earliest visible sign of both collagen loss and dehydration. Before reaching for stronger anti-aging actives, make sure you're consistently using a hydrating serum (hyaluronic acid), then introduce a low-strength retinoid a few nights a week for longer-term improvement.
concern_addon_notes.Greasy appearance: A generally greasy look throughout the day is usually a sebum-regulation issue rather than a hydration one. Blotting papers help short-term, but niacinamide and a lightweight gel moisturizer address the underlying oil production.
concern_addon_notes.Oily T-zone: An oily T-zone with normal or dry cheeks is the hallmark of combination skin. Apply oil-controlling ingredients (niacinamide, BHA) mainly to the forehead/nose/chin, and use a lighter touch with actives on the cheeks to avoid over-drying them.
concern_addon_notes.Peeling: Visible peeling usually signals that your barrier is irritated or over-exfoliated. Pause any acids, retinoids, or scrubs immediately and focus purely on gentle cleansing and barrier repair (ceramides, panthenol) until the peeling fully resolves, then reintroduce actives slowly.
concern_addon_notes.Rash: A rash, as distinct from general redness, can indicate an allergic reaction, contact dermatitis, or an underlying condition that this tool isn't designed to diagnose. Stop using any recently introduced products, and see a doctor if it doesn't clear within a few days or if it spreads, blisters, or is painful.
concern_addon_notes.Sagging skin: Sagging is primarily a collagen and skin-structure concern rather than a surface-level one. Topical peptides and retinoids can help modestly over months, but noticeable sagging is best discussed with a dermatologist, who can advise on in-clinic options like radiofrequency or ultrasound treatments.
concern_addon_notes.Skin irritation: General irritation is a sign your barrier needs support before adding more active ingredients. Simplify your routine down to a gentle cleanser and a barrier-repair moisturizer for at least a week, then reintroduce actives one at a time afterward.
concern_addon_notes.Whiteheads: Whiteheads are closed comedones, which respond well to ingredients that penetrate the pore lining, like salicylic acid or a low-strength adapalene. Avoid squeezing them - whiteheads sit deeper than blackheads, so squeezing carries a higher risk of scarring or spreading infection.
concern_addon_notes.default: This was flagged from your description alongside the main condition above - the routine for your main condition already covers general care, but mention this specifically if you consult a dermatologist.
